title: He spent years measuring how the Indian Ocean is warming. The world's largest Earth science society just gave him its top communications honor.

sources.text: Deccan Chronicle - Indian scientists among AGU 2026 awardees
ETV Bharat - Indian scientists among AGU 2026 awardees

caption:
He spent years measuring how the Indian Ocean is warming. The world's largest Earth science society just gave him its top communications honor.

The AGU is the world's largest Earth and space science society and the prize - named for Pavel S. Molchanov - is one of only 43 AGU honors awarded globally in 2026. It comes with a $25,000 award and will be presented at AGU's annual meeting in San Francisco this December.

Koll's research tracked the Indian Ocean's warming trend and its downstream effects - shifting monsoon patterns, intensifying cyclones and more frequent marine heatwaves - work that directly informs how India and its neighbors plan for climate risk. A second Indian scientist, Neelima Satyam of IIT-Indore, was named in the same 2026 AGU cohort for the Devendra Lal Memorial Medal.

A Viksit Bharat by 2047 has to be built with clear eyes about a warming ocean on its doorstep. Recognition like this signals Indian climate science isn't just documenting the problem - it's setting the terms the rest of the world uses to talk about it.
